lessons.title: 1. Counting Operations
lessons.description: Estimate work by counting loop iterations. Implement `linear_sum(n)` that sums 1..n in O(n) with an explicit loop.

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 4.2. for Statements — Looping Statements (Tutorial)

exercises.question:
What does this program print?

```python
def linear_sum(n):
    total = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        total += i
    return total

print(linear_sum(5))
```
exercises.explanation: range(1, 6) yields 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, which add to 15. 10 is what stopping one early (range(1, n)) gives; 21 is what one extra iteration (range(1, n + 2)) gives.

lessons.title: 2. Constant vs Linear Lookup
lessons.description: Compare list membership (O(n)) vs set membership (O(1) average). Implement `has_in_set(items, target)`.
learning_objectives: Use a set for average O(1) membership
lessons.solution_code:
def has_in_set(items, target):
    return target in set(items)

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — Time complexity of operations on built-in types — 'x in s' is O(1) for sets, O(n) for lists
